Definition: properly, to roil water; figuratively, to disturb or affict
BiblicalUsage: The verb means to stir up, to trouble, to roil the water. Jacob tells his sons they have troubled me to make me to stink among the inhabitants of the land; Joshua asks Achan, Why hast thou troubled us?; Jonathan says his father hath troubled the land; and Ahab greets Elijah with, Art thou he that troubleth Israel? In every case the trouble is real — and in every case the accuser has the wrong man, or the wrong reason.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the word's sting is in who says it. Ahab calls the prophet the troubler when Ahab himself is the trouble; Jacob blames his sons for a trouble he helped make. The Bible keeps turning the charge around: the real troubler is the sin, not the one who names it.
RelatedEvents: The Defeat at Ai and Achan's Sin; Dinah and Shechem
